To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two isoforms of melanopsin, melanopsin L (Opn4L) and melanopsin S (Opn4S) have distinct expression profiles in developing mouse retina.
two isoforms of mouse Melanopsin (Opn4L and 4S) are differentially expressed during postnatal development of the mouse retina.

the expression profiles of the two melanopsin isoforms are distinct during development of the mouse retina, with Opn4L levels increasing later than Opn4S levels, and we suggest that the differential expression of the two isoforms is associated with the functional and morphological maturation of the two pRGC subpopulations, M1 and M1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of melanopsin in the visual system.
the development of the visual system, and in particular with the development of light detection in the retina.
the development and function of the mammalian retina, with particular focus on the role of the photopigment melanopsin in the generation of circadian rhythms and pupillary reflexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differential expression of Opn1sw (melanopsin) isoforms (Opn4L and 4S) during postnatal development of the retina is associated with the functional differentiation of the M1 and M4 subtypes of p-RGCs.

the expression of Opn 4 L and Opn 4 S are differentially expressed during postnatal development and that the expression of these isoforms is associated with the functional and morphological maturation of M 1 and M 2 pRGCs respectively.

Opn4S is expressed at a high level at birth, whereas Opn4L is not expressed at all at this stage of development, and that the expression of both isoforms increases during postnatal development, reaching adult levels by P10 for Opn4S but P14-30 for Opn4L.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of the melanopsin gene is regulated by alternate splicing during postnatal development of the retina, with the two melanopsin isoforms, Opn4 L and Opn4 S, showing differential expression in the two types of melanopsin expressing ganglion cells (M1 and M2) during postnatal development.
Opn4S is the dominant melanopsin isoform in the neonate and is the first melanopsin isoforms to develop in the retina, whereas the Opn4L isoform is the predominant melanopsin isoforme in adult pRGCs.
Opn4L is a key factor for the development and functional maturation of the M2 type of pRGC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two different isoforms of melanopsin in the retina and they have different expression patterns.
there are differences in the developmental expression of the two melanopsin isoforms.
there is an increase in expression of melanopsin in pRGCs during development, with a differential profile of Opn4 isoforms being expressed.
